newsitem.title: USA: Simpson possible $440 mln sales for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Simpson possible $440 mln sales for 1997.

text.p: Simpson Industries inc said Wednesday it could possibly post sales of about $440 million for 1997.
"Simpson is ramping up new programs that will strengthen sales well into the next century," Roy Parrott, president and chief executive, said in a statement.

"If the domestic and international economies remain strong and there is no further deterioration in auto and truck production, we are looking at sales of about $440 million for 1997," Parrott said, adding the number includes the second half consolidation of sales with international expansion and the acquisition of the Vibration Attenuation business of Holset Engineering from Cummins Engine Co Inc.
A previously announced closure of the Jackson, Michigan plant should generate about $2.5 million of annualized savings, beginning in 1998, the company said.
Simpson on Wednesday reported second quarter net earnings of $0.30 a share versus $0.33 a share last year, which included about a $0.02 a share gain.
Strong sales to diesel engine customers and a new wheel-end and suspension program offset the effects of a decline in auto production and strikes at two key customers, the company said.
Simpson supplies powertrain and chassis products.
